summary: Remote-command agent: obfuscated WebSocket gateway drives shell/PTY execution on installer host
details: The package installs a daemon (bin `whalent`) that connects to a WebSocket gateway (default `wss://...` operated by the publisher) and, per its own README, 'accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) via the gateway'. It bundles `ws`, `ssh2`, `node-pty`, `child_process`, and a Jupyter sidecar that executes arbitrary Python read from stdin JSON, giving the remote gateway shell/PTY/exec sinks on the host running the agent. The main entry `dist/index.cjs` and the 13.6 MB `dist/core.cjs` are heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (1412-entry string array, control-flow flattening, 1801 decoder-wrapper inlines), which hides the network->shell dataflow and prevents review of what the gateway is permitted to invoke. `dist/core.cjs` also contains loopback references to RDP (127.0.0.1:3389) and VNC (127.0.0.1:5900, 5901), which the remote-driven agent could reach. The remote party holds control of a shell/PTY channel on the host; blast radius is full-host RCE on any machine running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
